product_offering.core_offering: Column is a nationally chartered bank that provides API-first programmable banking infrastructure for software companies and fintech platforms. Through a REST API, partners can create FDIC-insured bank accounts, issue cards, initiate ACH/wire/real-time/international payments, and originate, finance, or sell loans. The platform connects directly to the Federal Reserve, The Clearing House (RTP), FedNow, SWIFT, and card networks, and is licensed as Column N.A. to operate nationwide with over 800 partner banks in its FDIC sweep network.
product_offering.differentiator: Column is the only nationally chartered bank designed specifically for developers and software companies. Unlike traditional banks that use middleware and sponsor bank relationships, Column runs its own dedicated hardware connected directly to the Federal Reserve, TCH, and SWIFT. This 'close to the metal' approach provides granular control and eliminates vendor dependencies. The company is 100% founder and employee owned with no external investors, enabling focus on long-term customer value rather than growth metrics.
product_offering.functional_benefit: Real-time payment processing via RTP and FedNow networks; FDIC-insured deposits through 800+ partner bank sweep network; API-accessible bank accounts, cards, lending, and payment rails; 99.999% uptime guarantee; $4.5T+ annual transaction volume capacity; No. 1 position in US real-time payments
product_offering.problem_solved: Column solves the fundamental problem that fintech companies and software platforms face when trying to build financial products: the complexity and cost of partnering with traditional banks, dealing with multiple middleware providers, and navigating fragmented payment infrastructure. By providing a unified API-accessible banking platform with direct connections to payment networks, Column enables partners to embed banking, payments, and lending into their products without becoming a bank themselves.
quantifiable_outcome: No. 1 issuer of real-time payments in the US
product_offering.product_overview: Column is a nationally chartered bank built as API-first banking infrastructure for software companies, offering a unified platform with modular products across payments and lending. The platform operates through two main categories: Infrastructure products (ACH, Wire, Book Transfers, Ledger, Bank Accounts, Card Programs, Checks, Realtime Payments, and International Wires) that enable companies to move, hold, and lend dollars at scale; and Lending products (Loan Origination, Debt Financing, and Loan Purchase) that help companies offer and scale credit programs. All products are accessible via a REST API with direct connections to Federal Reserve, The Clearing House, SWIFT, and card networks (Visa, Mastercard). The company processes over $4.5 trillion in annual transaction volume with 99.999% uptime and serves as the banking backbone for fintech companies including Brex, Mercury, Ramp, and Best Egg.

icp.description: Primary ICP — neobanks, fintech startups, and software platforms needing programmable, API-accessible banking that scales with their products without having to build bank infrastructure or rely on sponsor-bank + middleware stacks. They use Column for FDIC-insured accounts, domestic/international payments, real-time rails (FedNow/RTP), and card programs. Buying is led by engineering and product leaders with fintech/platform executives sponsoring; decision dynamics are competitive/strategic as partners often migrate from legacy sponsor-bank arrangements to gain performance, control, and a national charter footprint. Sales cycle is long and multi-stakeholder with API-first self-service top-of-funnel and enterprise field sales close.

profiles.name: William Hockey
profiles.overview: Co-founder and CEO of Column; former Plaid co-founder who acquired Northern California National Bank in 2021 to obtain Column's national bank charter and built the company as banking infrastructure for software platforms.
profiles.profile_commentary: William Hockey is described as a hands-on engineering CEO who is also actively coding. He co-founded Plaid, the category-defining financial-data connectivity platform, before founding Column in 2019. His Plaid experience directly informs Column's developer-first positioning. He led the 2021 acquisition of Northern California National Bank to transform Column into a nationally chartered bank (Column N.A.) and personally champions the 100% founder/employee ownership model as a conscious trade-off favoring long-term customer value over venture-backed growth velocity.

recent_move.description: Acquired Northern California National Bank to obtain a national bank charter and transform into Column N.A., a nationally chartered bank purpose-built as banking infrastructure for software companies.
Launched Realtime Payments as a generally available product on RTP and FedNow rails, claiming the No. 1 position for real-time payments in the US after more than a year of customer production usage.

Launched the Credit at Column suite of capital products (warehouse lines, forward flows, loan retention) ranging from $5M to several hundred million, extending from origination into balance-sheet funding.

Rebuilt API documentation around a single OpenAPI source of truth, publishing in clean markdown and LLM-optimized HTML to position Column as the developer-banking platform best suited to AI-assisted integration.
Issued Bilt Card 2.0 in a four-party structure with Cardless and Fidem Financial, embedding Column in the consumer rewards/rent-payment vertical.
Hired an Emerging Markets Lead for MENA based in Dubai with regular regional travel and quarterly travel to SF headquarters, opening the first regional hub outside the United States.
Column N.A. acquired Northern California National Bank in 2021, enabling it to become a nationally chartered bank built as banking infrastructure for other companies.
recent_move.title: Acquisition of Northern California National Bank

expansion_highlight.description: Dedicated Emerging Markets Lead for MENA based in Dubai, with quarterly travel to San Francisco, signals formal entry into the Middle East and likely adjacent markets. Regional travel scope extends to Latin America and Central Asia per the same role.

October 2025 launch of Credit at Column (warehouse lines, forward flows, loan retention, $5M to several hundred million) extends Column from origination infrastructure into balance-sheet capital, creating a new revenue line and deepening wallet share with existing lending partners.

Recent partnerships move Column into new verticals beyond core fintech: private aviation (Hamilton AI, April 2026), order-to-cash/AR (Nuvo, March 2026), SMB financing (Affiniti, March 2026), installment lending in select states (Regional Management, March 2026), and consumer rewards (Bilt Card 2.0, January 2026).

Parafin/Visa and 360 Payments/Nav bring embedded-finance platforms and their SMB end-customers into Column's footprint, indicating a deliberate move down-market from direct enterprise deals into a platform-partner distribution model.

The OpenAPI-as-source-of-truth documentation rebuild, LLM-optimized publishing format, and developer self-service sandbox indicate a deliberate effort to make Column the most AI- and developer-discoverable bank, lowering future integration friction.

Dedicated Strategic Partnerships Leads for credit and payments formalize a channel-led enterprise motion, separating the largest direct integrations (Brex, Mercury, Ramp) from a scalable mid-market pipeline.
